title: Proper base change over a finite extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with $A=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $I=(\varpi)$, using [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] of noetherian finite-dimensional schemes $X,Y,X',Y'$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Assume $f$ and $f'$ are proper and that the geometric fibers of $f$ have dimension at most some $e\geq0$, as in [cor-weil-pbc-constructible-complete]. Use the raw rational categories $\Dbc(T,E)=\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)[1/\varpi]$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Denote by $Rf_*,Rf'_*,Lg^*,Lg'^*$ the rational extensions, as in [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport], of the integral direct images and completed pullbacks in that corollary. The specified rational exchange is the extension of its completed integral exchange. For every $K\in\Dbc(X,E)$ its component is an isomorphism
$$
 Lg^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*Lg'^*K
 \quad\text{in }\Dbc(Y',E).
$$

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], the raw rational category has exactly the objects of the integral category. Write the given $K$ as the rational image of its integral object $K_0$; no existence theorem for lattices is needed. By [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}<1$. By [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], the absolute value on $E$ restricts to this absolute value and $\mathfrak m_E=(\varpi)$. Consequently $\ell\in I$ and $\ell(A/I)=0$. Thus $N=\ell$ is a positive annihilator of $A/I$ invertible on all four schemes.

source.place: Proof, integral exchange followed by rationalization; expanded scalar and identity checks

proof.text: Apply [cor-weil-pbc-constructible-complete] to the given square and $K_0$. Its four noetherian finite-dimensional hypotheses, the properness of $f,f'$, and the geometric fiber bound $e$ are hypotheses of the item; its invertible annihilator is provided by step 1. It gives the specified integral natural isomorphism $\eta: Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rf_*\Rightarrow Rf'_*Lg'^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ on the integral constructible categories. In particular both values at $K_0$ lie in the integral category on $Y'$.

source.place: Proof, integral exchange followed by rationalization; expanded scalar and identity checks

proof.text: For the auxiliary squares below, identify identity operations first. Ordinary direct image along an identity map is the identity on module sheaves and on complexes, hence its derived functor is naturally the identity. By [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], along an identity the coefficient map $c_{\mathrm{id}}$ is the identity, so completed identity pullback is $\operatorname{Rlim}$ of the reduction tower $K_\bullet$, and its comparison $K\to\operatorname{Rlim}K_\bullet$ is the quotient-tower completion unit. Derived completeness in [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] means that the Koszul unit $\eta_K$ is invertible. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], for the completed coefficient sheaf the Koszul completion and $\operatorname{Rlim}_n(K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T)$ are canonically isomorphic respecting the units. Hence the quotient-tower unit is an isomorphism on derived-complete objects, and completed identity pullback is naturally the identity on each integral constructible category. These identifications respect shifts and triangles: for ordinary identity this is termwise equality, and the completion unit is induced by the quotient-tower maps, which commute with the shifts of complexes.

source.place: Proof, integral exchange followed by rationalization; expanded scalar and identity checks

proof.text: Check preservation and exactness of the four individual operations, rather than assuming these from preservation by the original composites. For $h=f$ and $h=f'$, apply [cor-weil-pbc-constructible-complete] to the square whose two vertical arrows are $h$ and whose horizontal arrows are identities. After step 3 its triangulated composites are naturally $Rh_*$, giving the required restriction and exactness. The fiber bound for $f'$ is $e$: for a geometric point $y':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y'$, the chosen cartesian identification [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] identifies its fiber with $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ for the geometric point $gy'$. For $h=g$ and $h=g'$, use instead the square with vertical identities and both horizontal arrows $h$. The corollary's composites are now naturally $Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$, so these also restrict and are exact. The vertical identities are proper with geometric fibers of dimension zero. Every auxiliary corner is one of the original schemes, and $N=\ell$ is still an invertible annihilator. Thus the corollary applies in all four cases.

source.place: Proof, integral exchange followed by rationalization; expanded scalar and identity checks

proof.text: Check scalar actions in the actual constructions. For $a\in A$, ordinary module direct image sends multiplication by $a$ to multiplication by its image in the target coefficient action, hence to multiplication by the same constant $a$. In [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] the reduction tensor and its tower maps do so as well: $(au)\otimes1=a(u\otimes1)$. In [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] the coefficient map is induced by the quotient projections, so it sends every constant $a$ to that same constant; inverse image and the subsequent extension of scalars therefore preserve these scalar maps. Ordinary inverse limit multiplies a compatible family componentwise, so it too preserves scalar maps. All these termwise operations are additive and preserve shifts and cone complexes, since a cone uses just two summands and the given differential. Finally [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category] makes localization of module complexes $A$-linear, so the same scalar equalities hold after passing to the ambient derived categories.

source.place: Proof, integral exchange followed by rationalization; expanded scalar and identity checks

proof.text:
For the left derived reduction and tower-pullback constructions of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], use their resolving-class comparison from [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. Write it as $\varepsilon_P:LF(QP)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(P)$ for a complex $P$ in the prescribed K-flat class. Naturality at $a\,\mathrm{id}_P$, and step 5, give
$$\varepsilon_P LF(Q(a\,\mathrm{id}_P))=F(a\,\mathrm{id}_P)\varepsilon_P=a\varepsilon_P.$$
By the $A$-linearity of $Q$ in [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category] and invertibility of $\varepsilon_P$, $LF(a\,\mathrm{id}_{QP})=a\,\mathrm{id}_{LF(QP)}$. Every input is isomorphic to some $QP$, using the resolving-class quasi-isomorphism. Conjugating by its image under $LF$ gives the same equality on every input. Therefore, for every morphism $u:C\to D$, $LF(au)=LF((a\,\mathrm{id}_D)u)=a LF(u)$. The cited resolving-class theorem also makes $LF$ exact, hence additive. This proves the required $A$-linearity without assuming a scalar-linear choice of resolutions or that arbitrary morphisms lift to maps between arbitrary K-flat complexes.

source.place: Proof, integral exchange followed by rationalization; expanded scalar and identity checks

proof.text:
For right derived direct image and inverse limit use [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]: the natural comparison $\rho_J:F(J)\xrightarrow{\sim}RF(QJ)$ is invertible on a K-injective representative $J$. The termwise functors are exact on homotopy categories by the cone calculation in step 5; their K-injective constructions are the integral direct image and the inverse limit of [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]. Naturality at $a\,\mathrm{id}_J$ gives
$$RF(Q(a\,\mathrm{id}_J))\rho_J=\rho_J F(a\,\mathrm{id}_J)=a\rho_J.$$
Using [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category], cancellation gives $RF(a\,\mathrm{id}_{QJ})=a\,\mathrm{id}_{RF(QJ)}$. Every input is isomorphic to such a $QJ$; conjugation gives the same identity there, and $RF(au)=RF((a\,\mathrm{id})u)=aRF(u)$. Additivity of direct image on the constructible categories is supplied by step 4, and additivity of derived inverse limit by its cited triangulated-functor statement. The reduction and pullback constructions in step 6, followed by this $A$-linear derived inverse limit, give $A$-linear completed pullbacks. Hence all four exact restricted functors of step 4 are $A$-linear.

source.place: Proof, integral exchange followed by rationalization; expanded scalar and identity checks

proof.text: Apply [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] to these four exact $A$-linear integral functors and the specified exchange $\eta$ from step 2. It gives their rational extensions and the natural exchange with component $\eta_{K_0}\otimes1$. The extension of a composite agrees with the composite of the extensions: on objects they agree, and on a pure tensor $u\otimes b$ both give $F(G(u))\otimes b$; equality follows on all morphisms by linearity. Thus this is precisely the rational exchange specified in the item, rather than merely an unspecified isomorphism between its endpoints.

source.place: Proof, integral exchange followed by rationalization; expanded scalar and identity checks

proof.text:
Set $v=\eta_{K_0}^{-1}$ in the integral category on $Y'$. Composition and identities in [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] give
$$(v\otimes1)(\eta_{K_0}\otimes1)=(v\eta_{K_0})\otimes1=\mathrm{id}\otimes1,$$
and likewise $(\eta_{K_0}\otimes1)(v\otimes1)=\mathrm{id}\otimes1$. Hence $v\otimes1$ is an inverse to the specified rational exchange. Step 1 covers every rational object, including zero and objects annihilated by a power of $\varpi$.
